rows.source: ORR safety-critical railway work and train protection
rows.verified: ROGS Part 4 contains requirements for competence, fitness and fatigue management in safety-critical railway work.

rows.source: ORR safety-critical railway work and train protection
rows.verified: Controllers of safety-critical work must explain how such work is managed within their safety-management arrangements.

rows.source: ORR safety-critical railway work and train protection
rows.verified: Safety-critical tasks must be carried out by competent people.

rows.source: ORR safety-critical railway work and train protection
rows.verified: Examples include driving, dispatching, signalling, component installation, maintenance and protecting people working on track.

rows.source: ORR safety-critical railway work and train protection
rows.verified: Train-protection systems reduce risks from signals passed at danger and overspeeding.

rows.source: ORR safety-critical railway work and train protection
rows.verified: Train-protection equipment can automatically apply train brakes when movement exceeds safe limits.

rows.source: ORR safety-critical railway work and train protection
rows.verified: At minimum, dutyholders must use a train-protection system capable of intervening and applying brakes as required by RSR99.

rows.source: ORR safety-critical railway work and train protection
rows.verified: ORR expects operators and infrastructure controllers to plan improvements and migration toward higher-level automatic train protection where reasonably practicable.

rows.source: ORR safety-critical railway work and train protection
rows.verified: Railway risk depends on task, competence, fitness, fatigue, signalling, train and infrastructure condition, protection and operating context.

rows.source: ORR safety-critical railway work and train protection
rows.verified: ORR evidence is worker-, train-, route-, system-, operation-, control- and time-specific and is not a parcel-level rail-incident probability.

rows.source: UK Civil Aviation Authority laser-attack safety
rows.verified: Laser illumination can distract or temporarily impair flight crew during high-workload phases of flight.

rows.source: UK Civil Aviation Authority laser-attack safety
rows.verified: Laser attacks occur near major airports but can also affect general aviation and emergency helicopters.

rows.source: UK Civil Aviation Authority laser-attack safety
rows.verified: Single-pilot operations are especially vulnerable because no second pilot may be available to take control.

rows.source: UK Civil Aviation Authority laser-attack safety
rows.verified: The CAA asks witnesses who see a laser being shone at an aircraft to contact the police.

rows.source: UK Civil Aviation Authority laser-attack safety
rows.verified: The Laser Misuse (Vehicles) Act 2018 provides criminal penalties for endangering aircraft with lasers.

rows.source: UK Civil Aviation Authority laser-attack safety
rows.verified: CAA safety material covers reporting, training and actions during and after a laser attack.

rows.source: UK Civil Aviation Authority laser-attack safety
rows.verified: Safety guidance applies to aircraft operators, pilots, air-traffic personnel, aerodromes and ground-service providers.

rows.source: UK Civil Aviation Authority laser-attack safety
rows.verified: Post-event guidance includes consideration of eye health and operational fitness after exposure.

rows.source: UK Civil Aviation Authority laser-attack safety
rows.verified: Laser-event risk depends on beam power, distance, cockpit exposure, phase of flight, crew composition, visibility and response.

rows.source: UK Civil Aviation Authority laser-attack safety
rows.verified: CAA laser evidence is event-, aircraft-, crew-, location-, phase-of-flight- and time-specific and is not a parcel-level aviation probability.

rows.source: OPSS unsafe-product alerts and recalls
rows.verified: OPSS publishes product safety alerts, reports and recalls for products that present health or safety risks.

rows.source: OPSS unsafe-product alerts and recalls
rows.verified: The product-recall service provides information for consumers, businesses and regulators.

rows.source: OPSS unsafe-product alerts and recalls
rows.verified: Market-surveillance and enforcement authorities must notify unsafe or noncompliant products through the Product Safety Database.

rows.source: OPSS unsafe-product alerts and recalls
rows.verified: Notification guidance covers both Great Britain and Northern Ireland market arrangements.

rows.source: OPSS unsafe-product alerts and recalls
rows.verified: OPSS validates and publishes product safety reports and product recalls where required.

rows.source: OPSS unsafe-product alerts and recalls
rows.verified: OPSS can share relevant product-safety information with overseas regulators.

rows.source: OPSS unsafe-product alerts and recalls
rows.verified: Product-safety notices can identify the product, risk, legal noncompliance and required corrective action.

rows.source: OPSS unsafe-product alerts and recalls
rows.verified: Consumers and businesses can use the alerts and recalls service to check current product-safety information.

rows.source: OPSS unsafe-product alerts and recalls
rows.verified: Product risk depends on model, design, manufacture, instructions, use, user group, defect, corrective action and market timing.

rows.source: OPSS unsafe-product alerts and recalls
rows.verified: OPSS evidence is product-, batch-, user-, market-, enforcement-, corrective-action- and time-specific and is not a parcel-level harm probability.
